 \label{pert:concentration-eq}$$ The assertion holds for the reservoir as well as for the original system. Constants need not be uniform in $L$ or $

 \label{pert:palm-bound}$$ For a fixed mark specification the function $H_N(t,u)$ is the same for all its types $j$: its base reservoir contains the full original Poisson families, including all types.

For every mark specification included in the perturbation family, old tree, anchor, and bounded overlap-polynomial test $f$, every Taylor coefficient at $t=0$ of $H_N(t,0)$ tends to zero along the selected sequence.

For the perturbation family defined above, along every sequence from Lemma 12, $$\sum_{E\in\mathfrak E(\mathcal T,a_*,\mathcal C)} c_E\,\mathbb E[fR_E] -\mathbb E f \sum_{E\in\mathfrak E(\{a_*\},a_*,\mathcal C)} c_E\,\mathbb E[R_E] \longrightarrow0. \label{pert:tree-identity-eq}$$ This holds for every fixed old tree, either kind of anchor, every bounded polynomial $f$ in its multioverlaps, every finite number of ordered added colors, and every prescribed constraint $\mathcal C$. The empty addition is allowed. The error is taken to zero at fixed $L$, fixed tree, and fixed constraint, before any limit in $L$.

For every fixed labeled topology $S$, $$\lim_{L\to\infty}\limsup_{N\to\infty}
       \mathcal A_{L,\eta}\operatorname{Var}(R_S)=0
       \qquad(\eta>0),
 \label{decor:overlap-concentration-equation}$$ where only the $b(S)$ branching depths are averaged. For a singleton, whose average has no coordinates, $\operatorname{Var}(R_S)\to0$ as $N\to\infty$ at every fixed $L$.

If a random vector $B\in[-1,1]^N$ is conditionally independent of $A_S$ given $\mathscr F_d$, then $$\bigl\|(A_S-\mu_{d,S})\cdot B\bigr\|_{L^2}
        \le v_N(S,d)^{1/4}.
 \label{decor:contraction-bound}$$ If $X,Y,Z$ are conditionally independent copies of a bounded random vector given a sigma field $\mathscr G$, and $C$ is its conditional covariance matrix, then $$\mathbb E(X\cdot Y-X\cdot Z)^2
       \ge \frac2{N^2}\mathbb E\sum_{i,j}C_{ij}^2.
 \label{decor:three-copy-bound}$$

Fix a topology $S$ and a subset $U$ of its branching vertices. For each $\eta$-regular depth assignment, let $S^U$ have the same topology with the depths of the vertices in $U$ increased by one. At an ancestral evaluation depth $d$, compare the means using the same sampled prefix. Then, for all sufficiently large $L$, $$\mathcal A_{L,\eta}\mathbb E
       \|\mu_{d,S^U}-\mu_{d,S}\|_N^2\le C/L.
 \label{decor:branch-depth-continuity}$$ The average ranges over all branching depths; the coordinate $d$ is also averaged if it ranges, and otherwise is held fixed. If $d$ ranges along an initial unary stretch of $S$, then $$\mathcal A_{L,\eta}\mathbb E
       \|\mu_{d+1,S}-\mu_{d,S}\|_N^2\le C/L,
 \label{decor:evaluation-depth-continuity}$$ where this average includes $d$ and all branching depths, and the means are evaluated along the same sampled path. The constant depends only on the number of vertices and shifts, uniformly in $N$, the evaluation depth, and the transition kernels.

For each fixed $N$, $L\ge2$, and selected parameter vector, with the reservoir root disorder averaged, there is a deterministic trial law $\zeta_{L,N}\in\mathcal M_L$ whose single-label spin process has the same expected spin products on every prescribed tree as a uniformly chosen site of the reservoir. Different trial labels can be chosen independently.

Fix a prescribed tree with $k$ leaves. Suppose an observable of absolute value at most one uses the replica-spin patterns at $a$ independent uniform site labels. Replacing these patterns by $a$ independent trial-label patterns from 22 changes its expected value by at most $$\label{comp:pattern-error} a\sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq[k]}\mathbb E|R_S-\mathbb ER_S|.$$ The observable may also depend on new insertion disorder, independent of the reservoir.
For every bounded permutation-invariant interaction law and bounded field law, with the functionals defined in 2, $$\liminf_{N\to\infty}F_N\ge\inf_{r\ge0}\Phi_r.$$

Fix an even integer $p\ge2$, $\alpha>0$, and independent real random variables $J,H$ such that $J$ has a symmetric distribution and $\mathbb E|J|+\mathbb E|H|<\infty$. For every $\beta>0$, the model with $$\theta_\beta(s_1,\ldots,s_p)=\beta J\prod_{\ell=1}^p s_\ell, \qquad h_\beta=\beta H$$ satisfies the variational formula [main:formula], with the trial functional evaluated at these interaction and field laws. In particular, this holds for the Viana–Bray model (Viana and Bray 1985) [[VB85](#ref-VB85)], which is the case $p=2$.

Fix an even integer $K\ge2$ and $\alpha>0$. Let $\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_K$ be independent fair signs and let $W\ge0$ be independent of the signs, with $\mathbb EW<\infty$. For every $\beta>0$, the interaction $$\theta_\beta(s_1,\ldots,s_K) =-\beta W\prod_{\ell=1}^K\frac{1+\varepsilon_\ell s_\ell}{2}, \qquad h=0,$$ satisfies [main:formula]. The choice $W=1$ is the soft random even-$K$ SAT model; $W$ gives an independent nonnegative clause weight.
